title: Squeeze Enrichment of Intact Cells from Marine Sponge Tissues
author: Jose Lopez

steps.title: Prepare Sponge Tissue
steps.instruction: Cut a piece of sponge mesohyl (tissue) approximately 1-2 cm3 using a sterile scalpel and forceps and place it in a sterile petri dish.

substeps.instruction: If using frozen sponge pieces, thaw only enough to slice to prevent cell lysis.

steps.title: Soak Tissue in L Buffer
steps.instruction: Drip 1-3 ml of L buffer (10 mM Tris, pH 7.6, 100 mM EDTA, 20 mM NaCl) on top of the sponge tissue in the petri dish.

steps.title: Mince Tissue
steps.instruction: Mince the tissue as small as possible using the sterile scalpel and forceps.

steps.title: Squeeze Mesohyl
steps.instruction: Squeeze or press the mesohyl pieces with forceps against the bottom of the petri dish to expel the cellular interior contents into the L buffer.

steps.title: Collect and Centrifuge Cells
steps.instruction: Collect the cells (~3 ml) into microcentrifuge tubes and centrifuge.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at top speed (10,000g) for 30 seconds.
Alternatively, centrifuge at half speed if live cells are required for downstream use beyond DNA extraction.

steps.title: Recover Cell Pellet
steps.instruction: Decant the supernatant and save the pellet containing sponge and microbial cells.

steps.title: Rinse Petri Dish
steps.instruction: Rinse any remaining cells from the dish using an additional 1 ml of L buffer.

substeps.instruction: Mix the rinse with the original tubes.
Decant the supernatant and save the pellet.

steps.title: Final Pellet Preparation
steps.instruction: Perform a final spin and prepare the pellet for storage.

substeps.instruction: Remove remaining supernatant with a pipet.
Leave 10-20 ul of L buffer on the pellet before frozen storage.
